Let the common ratio in the Law of Sines be \(R\):

\[
a=R\sin\phi,\quad b=R\sin(135^\circ-\phi),\quad c=R\sin45^\circ
\]

where \(\tan\phi=\frac17\), so

\[
\sin\phi=\frac{1}{5\sqrt2},\qquad \cos\phi=\frac{7}{5\sqrt2}.
\]

Then

\[
\sin(135^\circ-\phi)=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}(\cos\phi+\sin\phi)
=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\cdot \frac{8}{5\sqrt2}
=\frac45.
\]

Thus the perimeter is

\[
R\left(\frac{1}{5\sqrt2}+\frac45+\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\right)
=R\left(\frac{4+3\sqrt2}{5}\right)
=24+18\sqrt2=6(4+3\sqrt2).
\]

So \(R=30\). Therefore

\[
AB=c=R\sin45^\circ=30\cdot \frac{\sqrt2}{2}=15\sqrt2.
\]

The altitude from \(B\) to \(AC\) is

\[
h=AB\sin\angle BAC = 15\sqrt2\cdot \frac{1}{5\sqrt2}=3.
\]

\[
\boxed{3}
\]
